areas.summary: Strong publicly visible evidence for enrichment and extra-curricular activity (8 specific items). Listed provision includes coding, for example in pe.

signals.text: Pupils participate in weekly extra-curricular activities including arts and crafts, sport, coding and catch-up interventions.
Science is sequenced throughout the year to ensure that children have opportunities to revisit learning across different contexts and make links with prior learning, for example in PE, and PSHE.
Visit from Ringway On Wednesday 11th December our students were visited by representatives, including 3 apprentices, from the highway services company, Ringway.

Pupils who are happy and healthy will find learning easier, be able to concentrate better, have more energy and, because of this, PE and extra-curricular sports clubs are held in high regard at Burstow Park School.

Implementation Pupils are taught twice a week in class groups; they learn the key skills needed and are given plenty of opportunities to practice and enjoy taking part in a wide range of sports throughout the year; these include ball skills, striking and fielding games and racket sports.

areas.summary: Strong publicly visible evidence for ethos and values (6 specific items). Listed provision includes art.

signals.text: The Blended Learning Suite is housed in a fully refurbished and self-contained provision with its own garden area; it offers a 1:1, 1:2 and small group (2:4) learning environment, all within a nurturing, low-arousal and predictable environment.
signals.pageTitle: Burstow Park School - Blended Learning Suite

signals.text: Each class in school keeps their own portfolio which records responses to art, photos of work and any involvement in whole- school or community projects, engaging with a variety of art forms, to explore values, attitudes, feelings and meanings.

areas.summary: Moderate publicly visible evidence for behaviour and pastoral care (5 specific items). Listed provision includes citizenship.

signals.text: The reasons for this will vary and can, for example, range from pupils having very high levels of anxiety or hyper-sensory needs, to there being a need to develop positive behaviours for learning before transferring to our main school site.
signals.pageTitle: Burstow Park School - Blended Learning Suite

signals.text: Our scheme of work supports the active development of a school culture that prioritises physical and mental health and wellbeing, providing students with skills to evaluate and understand their own wellbeing needs, practise self-care and contribute positively to the wellbeing of those around them.

areas.narrativeSummary: The reasons for this will vary and can, for example, range from pupils having very high levels of anxiety or hyper-sensory needs, to there being a need to develop positive behaviours for learning before transferring to our main school site.

areas.summary: Moderate publicly visible evidence for SEND and inclusion (4 specific items). Themes include access, differentiat, ehcp, inclusion.

signals.text: Each child who comes to Burstow Park School is treated as an individual; almost all our pupils have an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP), which will be used to inform our staff, enabling us to provide a holistic and bespoke approach to the education, care and wellbeing of pupils.

Literacy is also a key component of science; however, we use effective differentiation to ensure that pupils can access age- appropriate content, regardless of their literacy levels, to build and sustain high engagement and appropriate challenge of the subject content.

Understanding Ambition Opportunity
‘Hello’ From Our Proprietor
I am pleased to welcome you to the Burstow Park Group of schools . The Burstow Park Group of schools is the product of over 25 years of working with children who have special educational needs or disabilities, and their families. With a passion for personalised learning and working in a child-centred way, I have been able to use my wealth of experience as a consultant to Local Authorities to develop an educational provision which meets the true needs of children and families, especially where mainstream education is not easily accessible to them.
Testimonials
"This is definitely the school I am supposed to be at!" Member of Staff
Why Choose Us?
We offer education, of course, but in a relaxed, calm setting where children can feel comfortable. We even have our own Emotional Support Animal – a lovely, gentle miniature dachshund named Beanz.
Thursday 3rd September 2025
School re-opens for all students at 9.00am, including Redhill and Blended Learning

pageCache.pageTitle: Burstow Park School - Blended Learning Suite
pageCache.text:
Blended Learning Suite
Our Blended Learning Suite, which moved to the main site in November 2025, offers an alternative pathway for students who are not yet able to access full-time, on-site provision from day 1 of a placement. The reasons for this will vary and can, for example, range from pupils having very high levels of anxiety or hyper-sensory needs, to there being a need to develop positive behaviours for learning before transferring to our main school site.
We offer a fully bespoke and tailored transition into full-time school. Students develop skills to be active and successful learners, alongside a fully differentiated and bespoke curriculum which addresses gaps in learning, pre-teaches key concepts in readiness for successful learning and instils learner confidence. The Blended Learning Pathway has three separate aspects - one third is delivered face to face on-site through 1:1 and small group teaching, one third is delivered remotely via Teams or Google Classroom and one third is independent learning set by the student’s personal tutor.
Students enrolled with us benefit from a personalised timetable with a mixture of on-site provision (1:1 or 1:2 as required) and remotely delivered learning. The aim is to support your child to be able to successfully access full-time, on-site provision at our main school within a timescale that is achievable for them. Once a child is at the stage of being able to access full-time, they are supported to transition to our main school site.
The Blended Learning Suite is housed in a fully refurbished and self-contained provision with its own garden area; it offers a 1:1, 1:2 and small group (2:4) learning environment, all within a nurturing, low-arousal and predictable environment. Led by highly qualified and experienced staff, we are able to meet the needs of students who have a range of educational and social needs, using evidenced-based, contemporary and high-quality teaching methods.

As part of our careers and opportunities offer to pupils, we plan to invite a range of local and national company representatives to visit us at Burstow Park School.
Visit from Ringway
On Wednesday 11th December our students were visited by representatives, including 3 apprentices, from the highway services company, Ringway.
Students were given the opportunity to prepare a model road, ahead of roadworks taking place. Using miniature road cones, road signs and barrier fencing, the students worked together to ensure an area of the road could be fixed safely by the construction operatives, as well as ensuring road users were given timely warning of road works taking place.
Another activity required one student to act as the site supervisor, reading instructions carefully and providing steps and information for the other students in their team, who worked together to fix a broken gulley.
All students who took part learnt a great deal about the roles and responsibilities on offer at Ringway and there were great questions asked about the Ringway apprenticeship scheme.
Visit from Balfour Beatty
On Friday the 18th October our students were visited by representatives from the construction business Balfour Beatty.
They listened to a presentation about the roles, responsibilities and important work carried out by Balfour Beatty and learnt about a variety of jobs. These ranged from painting white lines on roads to operating drones to view wide areas of the land before, during and after a road or bridge has been built.
After the presentation, the students then had the opportunity to operate and fly a drone for themselves. We have some very skilful drone operators in the making at Burstow Park School and perhaps the visit has inspired some of our students to consider a career in construction in the future.

SEND
HOW WILL MY CHILD’S SPECIAL EDUCATIONAL NEEDS BE MET?
Each child who comes to Burstow Park School is treated as an individual; almost all our pupils have an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP), which will be used to inform our staff, enabling us to provide a holistic and bespoke approach to the education, care and wellbeing of pupils.
We have a safeguarding team, a SENCO team, a pastoral and inclusion team, as well as our teaching and teaching assistant teams. Our highly experienced Leadership and Senior Subject Teachers will ensure that appropriate literacy and numeracy interventions are put in place and that progress is effectively monitored.
It is normal for most young people to experience worries, such as those surrounding developing friendships, navigating the cyber world, relationships, fitting in, etc. The nurturing, safe, structured environment at Burstow Park will help to alleviate these worries as each pupil becomes part of the whole-school community. We provide an open and inclusive environment in which being different, being an individual, is welcomed.
